verses.text: Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense I’m making to you now.
When they heard him speaking to them in Hebrew, they grew even quieter. Then he said:

“I’m a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but I grew up here in this city. I studied at Gamaliel’s feet and was trained carefully in the law handed down by our ancestors. I was zealous for God, just as all of you are today.
I hunted down the people of this Way to the point of death. I arrested both men and women and put them in prison.

The high priest and the whole council of elders can confirm this. They gave me letters for our fellow Jews, and I went to Damascus to arrest the believers there and bring them back to Jerusalem for punishment.
“As I traveled and came close to Damascus, around noon a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed all around me.
I fell to the ground and heard a voice say, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’
I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He told me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, the one you are persecuting.’
The people with me saw the light and were frightened, but they didn’t understand the voice speaking to me.
I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ The Lord said, ‘Get up and go into Damascus. There you’ll be told everything God has appointed you to do.’
I couldn’t see because the light was so brilliant, so my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.
A man named Ananias came to me. He was devoted to the law and respected by all the Jews living in Damascus.
He stood beside me and said, ‘Brother Saul, see again!’ At that very moment, I looked up and could see him.
He said, ‘The God our ancestors worshiped chose you to know his will, to see the Righteous One, and to hear his voice.
You’ll be his witness to everyone, telling them what you’ve seen and heard.
So what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and have your sins washed away as you call on the Lord’s name.’
“Later, after I returned to Jerusalem, I was praying in the temple when I fell into a trance.
I saw the Lord telling me, ‘Leave Jerusalem quickly. They won’t accept your testimony about me.’
I said, ‘Lord, they know I went through the synagogues, throwing believers in prison and beating them.
When Stephen, your witness, was killed, I stood there approving. I even watched the clothes of the men who murdered him.’
“But the Lord said to me, ‘Go. I’m sending you far away to the Gentiles.’”
The crowd listened until he said that. Then they shouted, “Get rid of this man! He shouldn’t be allowed to live!”
They kept shouting, waving their cloaks around and throwing dust into the air.
The commander ordered Paul taken into the barracks. He told the soldiers to question him under a whipping, trying to find out why the crowd was yelling like this.
As they stretched him out to tie him for the whipping, Paul asked the centurion standing nearby, “Is it lawful to whip a Roman citizen who hasn’t been found guilty?”
When the centurion heard that, he went to the commander and warned him, “Be careful what you do. This man is a Roman citizen!”
The commander came to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” Paul said, “Yes.”
The commander replied, “I paid a lot for my citizenship.” Paul said, “I was born a citizen.”
Right away, the men who were about to question Paul backed off. The commander was alarmed when he realized he had put a Roman citizen in chains.

The next day, the commander wanted to learn exactly why the Jews were accusing Paul. He released him from his chains and ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he brought Paul down and set him before them.
